previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of systolic heart failure, ischemic cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and obesity, was admitted for acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbated by missing two days of torsemide during travel. He presented with worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, 10 kg weight gain, and lower extremity edema. Treatment included IV furosemide, which led to a weight reduction from 140 kg to 132 kg. His symptoms improved, though mild fluid overload persisted. Due to his preference for early discharge, he was transitioned to oral torsemide 160 mg daily, with increased hydralazine for blood pressure control. His creatinine rose to 2.3, consistent with baseline, likely due to diuresis. He was discharged home with compression stockings, strict medication adherence counseling, and a plan for close outpatient follow-up to monitor renal function and adjust diuretic therapy as needed.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

It was a pleasure caring for you at ___. You were admitted for 
difficulty breathin, weight gain and worsening leg swelling. You 
were found to have too much fluid in your body, because of your 
congestive heart failure. You were treated with IV  and oral 
diuretics and your symptoms improved. Your weight on admission 
was 137kg and it improved to 129kg at discharge. You should 
continue taking all of your heart failure medications at home, 
particularly your Torsemide (diuretic), to keep your weight 
down. You should weigh yourself every morning and call your 
Cardiologist if your weight goes up by more than 3lbs. If you 
experience chest pain, shortness of breath, worsening leg 
swelling, please call your doctor immediately or seek care in 
the Emergency Department.

It was wonderful to meet you and we wish you all the best in 
your recovery.

Sincerely,
Your medical team
